## Closes https://github.com/elastic/connectors-py/issues/###

Background
Currently, the SharePoint connector does not properly process files and folders that are shared with the "Everyone Except External Users" group. This group has a unique loginName format:c:0-.f|rolemanager|spo-grid-all-users

This login name is not recognized by the _access_control_for_member() function, which currently only supports:

c:0o.c|federateddirectoryclaimprovider|
c:0t.c|tenant|
As a result, these permissions are skipped, and the _access_control_list field remains incomplete, causing the documents to miss appropriate access metadata.

Problem
Documents or folders with permissions granted to the "Everyone Except External Users" group are being ignored by the connector, leading to inaccurate access control metadata.

Task
Modify the SharePoint connector to correctly process and include the "Everyone Except External Users" group when encountered.

Required Changes
Detect when a member has the login name: c:0-.f|rolemanager|spo-grid-all-users
Map it to a standard identifier in _allow_access_control, for example: group:EveryoneExceptExternalUsers
Update the logic in the async def _access_control_for_member(self, member): function to support this case.

Acceptance Criteria
The connector must:
Recognize the spo-grid-all-users login name.
Add the mapped identifier (group:EveryoneExceptExternalUsers) to the _allow_access_control field in the document metadata.
Ensure existing logic for federated and tenant groups is unaffected.

body:
This PR implements comprehensive improvements to the Shreads Chrome extension's notification system, providing users with granular control over notifications and subscription-based filtering as requested in the issue.

## Key Features Implemented

### 1. **Subscription-Based Feed Notifications**
The extension now only sends new feed notifications for webpages that users have subscribed to. This eliminates notification spam from unsubscribed sites while ensuring users stay updated on content they care about.

```javascript
// Only notify for subscribed rooms
const isSubscribed = await window.api.checkUserSubscription(room.roomId, userEmail);
if (!isSubscribed) {
  return; // Skip notification
}
```

### 2. **Modern Toggle Switch UI**
Replaced all checkbox-based settings with sleek iOS-style toggle switches for a more intuitive and modern user experience.

### 3. **Granular Notification Controls**
Added fine-grained notification settings allowing users to control exactly what notifications they receive:

- **전체 알림 ON/OFF** - Master toggle for all notifications
- **새 피드 알림** - New feed notifications (subscription-based)
- **내 피드 좋아요 알림** - Likes on user's feeds
- **내 댓글 좋아요 알림** - Likes on user's comments  
- **내 피드 댓글 알림** - Comments on user's feeds

### 4. **Smart Master Toggle**
The master toggle intelligently controls all granular settings - when disabled, it visually dims and disables individual notification toggles, providing clear visual feedback about the notification state.

## Screenshots

**Enhanced Notification Settings (Enabled):**
![Notifications Enabled](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/932ed4f2-f1cc-4314-abd1-895fb94400fa)

**Master Toggle Disabled State:**

**Consistent Toggle Design in General Settings:**
![General Settings](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5965cfee-c9c4-4490-a2c5-3ae8bd8ffa3d)

## Technical Implementation

- **Enhanced Data Structure**: Extended notification settings with granular controls while maintaining backward compatibility
- **Subscription Integration**: Leverages existing subscription API to filter notifications
- **CSS Toggle Components**: Custom toggle switch styling with smooth animations and disabled states
- **Error Handling**: Robust handling of API failures to ensure notifications work even when backend is unavailable

## User Experience Improvements

- **Reduced Notification Noise**: Users only receive notifications from subscribed content
- **Intuitive Controls**: Modern toggle switches are more accessible than checkboxes
- **Clear Visual Hierarchy**: Master toggle clearly controls sub-settings with visual feedback
- **Detailed Descriptions**: Each setting includes helpful descriptions of what it controls

This implementation perfectly addresses the requirements for "웹페이지별 구독 및 알림 세분화 기능 개선" by providing both subscription-based filtering and granular notification controls with an improved UI.

Fixes #60.

The fix works by disabling the vertex position optimization code for datasets where all layers are transformed.
Previously a dataset where all layers had transforms had `representativeMagForVertexAlignment=[1,1,1]` regardless of the zooming of the user. This caused the vertices of the plane to be bucket aligned to mag 1 buckets by the optimization code. The calculated bucket positions were then disregarded in the fragment shader but lead to the "blank" areas. Because when zoomed out, there were not enough vertices to cover all buckets in mag 1 regarding the viewed area leaving gaps in what was rendered.
This should now be fixed.

body:
### Summary Function to let you run a Javascript function on an HTML panel from Lua without having to deal with complex messy injection issues. _See #2328 for previous development progress._ ### Example As an example, the loading screen panel currently uses this: ```lua pnlLoading.JavascriptRun = string.format( [[if ( window.GameDetails ) GameDetails( "%s", "%s", "%s", %i, "%s", "%s", %.2f, "%s", "%s" );]], servername:JavascriptSafe(), serverurl:JavascriptSafe(), mapname:JavascriptSafe(), maxplayers_visible, steamid:JavascriptSafe(), gamemode:JavascriptSafe(), GetConVarNumber( "snd_musicvolume" ), GetConVarString( "gmod_language" ):JavascriptSafe(), niceGamemode:JavascriptSafe() ) self.HTML:RunJavascript( str ) ``` Using the new function from this PR, you could instead do this: ```lua self.HTML:RunFunction( "GameDetails", servername, serverurl, mapname, maxplayers_visible, steamid, gamemode, GetConVarNumber( "snd_musicvolume" ), GetConVarString( "gmod_language" ), niceGamemode ) ``` _This is not a suggestion to update the loading screen with this, it's just an example of how it's easier for developers._ ### About The function is available as both `RunFunction()` and `QueueFunction()`, the only difference is internally it calls either [RunJavascript()](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Panel:RunJavascript) or [QueueJavascript()](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/DHTML:QueueJavascript) respectively with the prepared javascript. Syntax is `html:QueueFunction( javascript function name to call, varargs to pass to it )` eg running `html:QueueFunction( "myfunc", "hello world", true, 10/2, game.GetMap() )` will execute `myfunc( "hello world", true, 5, "gm_flatgrass" );` in the javascript. Arguments support the following data types: Booleans, Numbers, Colours, Tables, and Strings. Some additional notes on data type handling: - Colours are converted by `:ToHex()` to strings. eg if you provide `Color(255,0,255,255)` the JS function will receive string `"#ff00ff"`, or if you provide `Color(255,0,255,153)` the JS function will receive string `"#ff00ff99"` - Tables (and table-like) are converted to json objects with `util.TableToJSON`. They can be read in JS eg `ply["rank"]`, `ghosts[0]["time"]`, `pos["x"]`, etc - Any other types are converted to string and protected by [JavascriptSafe](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/string.JavascriptSafe) ## Demo
[Click to view demo, including sample code and output] Here is a test panel to demonstrate functionality - [htmltest.lua](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/29847195/htmltest.lua.txt) Please try running it along with this PR to see functionality. concommand `htmltest` will open the panel. if you edit the code with autorefresh, run `htmltest` again and it'll regenerate the panel. Here are some examples from the test code: ### Works for native JS functions ```lua html:QueueFunction( "console.log", "'hello world!' is a mandatory reference to make in any demo." ) ``` > ### Works for custom JS functions, and multiple parameters lua: ```lua html:QueueFunction( "GameInfo", LocalPlayer():Name(), game.GetMap(), engine.ActiveGamemode() ) ``` Javascript: ```js function GameInfo(player, map, gamemode) { var div = document.createElement("div"); div.innerHTML = "Player is on map in gamemode "; div.querySelector(".ply").innerText = player; div.querySelector(".map").innerText = map; div.querySelector(".gm").innerText = gamemode; document.body.appendChild(div); } ``` Output: > ### Tables / Json ```lua html:QueueFunction( "ExplainJson", { [ "hero" ] = "freeman", [ "villain" ] = "combine", [ "episode" ] = 3 } ) ``` > ### Demo of various types ```lua html:QueueFunction( "ExplainType", "this is a string" ) html:QueueFunction( "ExplainType", true ) html:QueueFunction( "ExplainType", false ) html:QueueFunction( "ExplainType", 1234 ) html:QueueFunction( "ExplainType", -2/3 ) html:QueueFunction( "ExplainType", Color( 255, 0, 255, 255 ) ) html:QueueFunction( "ExplainType", Color( 255, 0, 255, 153 ) ) ``` > ### Demo of choosing to send a table depending on use ```lua html:QueueFunction( "ExplainType", Color( 255, 0, 255, 153 ) ) -- gets sent as a CSS hex string "#ff00ff99" html:QueueFunction( "ExplainType", Color( 255, 0, 255, 153 ):ToTable() ) -- gets sent as json object [255, 0, 255, 153], so you can access individual values ``` >
Suggestions and improvements are welcome. Thanks to @Grocel, @bloodycop6385, and @WinterPhoenix for feedback and reviews in #2328

## Summary
This PR fixes multiple critical issues with lockfile version management, addressing problems with stale versions persisting after configuration changes and incorrect handling of version upgrades.

## Problems Fixed

### 1. Stale versions persisting after removal from configuration
When versions were removed from the configuration, they would incorrectly remain in the lockfile, causing inconsistency between the configuration and lockfile state.

### 2. Version upgrades keeping both old and new versions
When `mise up` upgraded a tool (e.g., from 1.0.0 to 1.1.0), the lockfile would incorrectly contain both versions instead of just the upgraded version.

### 3. Platform information not being preserved
When updating existing tool versions, fresh platform information from new versions wasn't being properly merged.

### 4. Partial reinstalls losing other versions
When using multiple version constraints and partially reinstalling tools, the lockfile would lose track of non-reinstalled versions.

## Solution
Completely refactored the lockfile update logic to:
1. Properly replace old versions with upgraded ones when requests match
2. Preserve legitimate multiple versions when specified in configuration
3. Remove stale versions that no longer match any configuration request
4. Correctly merge platform information during updates
5. Use BTreeMap for consistent ordering in lockfile output

## Changes

## Summary

This PR implements a universal message field pattern across all AdCP task responses, addressing issue #16 about brief expectations and making the protocol more conversational and AI-friendly.

## Changes

### 1. Brief Expectations Enhancement (#16)
- Added conversational brief handling to `get_products`
- Introduced `clarification_needed` field for incomplete briefs
- Created guidelines for complete briefs while maintaining natural language flexibility
- Publishers can now request clarification instead of returning suboptimal results

### 2. Universal Message Field Pattern
Added `message` as the first field in all task responses:

```json
{
  "message": "Human-readable summary of the response",
  "context_id": "ctx-123",
  // ... structured data
}
```

Applied to all tasks:
- **Media Buy**: get_products, create_media_buy, add_creative_assets, check_media_buy_status, get_media_buy_delivery, update_media_buy, list_creative_formats
- **Signals**: get_signals, activate_signal

### 3. Documentation Updates
- Updated all task documentation with message examples
- Updated API reference for consistency
- Created design decision document explaining the pattern
- Added implementation guides with code examples

## Benefits

1. **AI-Native**: Agents can quickly understand responses without parsing JSON
2. **Human-Friendly**: Clear summaries for sales, support, and approvers
3. **Conversational**: Enables natural back-and-forth interactions
4. **Progressive Disclosure**: Read message for quick understanding, parse data for details
5. **Backward Compatible**: All structured data remains unchanged

## Examples

### Clarification Request
```json
{
  "message": "I'd be happy to help find the right products for your campaign. Could you share your budget and campaign timing?",
  "clarification_needed": true,
  "products": []
}
```

### Success Response
```json
{
  "message": "Successfully created your $50,000 media buy targeting pet owners in CA and NY. Upload creatives by January 30 to activate.",
  "media_buy_id": "mb_123",
  "status": "pending_activation"
}
```

## Testing

- All TypeScript checks pass
- Documentation builds successfully
- Examples demonstrate various response scenarios

When working on multiple features in parallel, e.g. during trunk based development, a single memory bank becomes a source of headache.

Keeping a single memory bank for multiple features at the same time distracts the LLM by providing far too many options, alternatives, constraints and goals.

Thus, this PR introduces feature focussed memory banks. The active memory bank can be toggled.

The concept adopts the idea of Rule Banks described in the Cline Bot documentation:

This PR refactors the permission user assignment functionality based on user feedback, moving user management from the creation modal to dedicated permission detail pages for better user experience and workflow separation.

## What Changed

**Before**: Users could assign other users to permissions directly during the permission creation process through a checkbox list in the creation modal.

**After**: 
- Permission creation is now streamlined with only essential fields (name, resource, action, description)
- User assignment is moved to dedicated permission detail pages
- Permission names in the data table are now clickable links to their detail pages

## Key Features

**Simplified Permission Creation:**
- Removed user selection interface from creation modal for cleaner, focused experience
- Reduced modal complexity and improved creation workflow
- Users can now create permissions without immediately needing to assign them

**New Permission Detail Pages:**
- Dedicated page for each permission showing detailed information
- User management interface similar to organization detail pages
- Email-based user search and assignment functionality
- View all users who currently have the permission
- Remove users from permissions with confirmation

**Enhanced Navigation:**
- Permission names in the index table are now clickable links
- Easy navigation from list view to detailed permission management
- Breadcrumb navigation back to permission index

## Technical Implementation

- **Preserved RBAC Architecture**: Maintains role-based permission system with automatic role creation/management
- **Improved UX**: Separates permission creation from user assignment for better workflow
- **Comprehensive Testing**: Added full test coverage for new detail page and user assignment functionality
- **Consistent Design**: Follows existing patterns established by organization detail pages

The refactoring improves the user experience by separating concerns: permission creation remains quick and simple, while user management gets dedicated space with full functionality for ongoing administration.

Addresses feedback from #66.
